overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair has discretion over public comment, the Commission could vote without first taking public comment, and the plan was not required to be available at the meeting. Resolved by informal action.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission did not allow public participation at its July 9 meeting before approving a landscape plan.
allegations.key_passage: The law does not require that a public body allow public participation, but rather gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission voted to approve the landscape plan without first taking public comment on it, over an objection from a member of the public.
allegations.key_passage: It is not a violation of the Open Meeting Law for a public body to vote on a topic without first taking comments from the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair limited public participation during the July 9 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting by limiting public participation during the meeting, as it is within the Chair’s discretion to do so.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the landscape plan was not available for review by the public during the July 9 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Absent a specific request for documents used at a meeting, the Commission is not obligated to make such documents available at a meeting to those members of the public in attendance.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
